title: Graph Neural Network Force Fields for Spin Dynamics in Metallic Magnets
authors: Ali Rayat, Yunhao Fan, Gia-Wei Chern
abstract: Metallic magnets exhibit complex spin dynamics governed by electronically generated interactions. Predictive simulations of such dynamics typically require repeated solutions of an underlying electronic problem throughout the time evolution, creating a major computational bottleneck. Here we introduce a graph neural network (GNN) magnetic force-field framework that learns the effective magnetic energy functional governing itinerant spin dynamics directly from electronic calculations. Conceptually analogous to machine-learned interatomic potentials, the proposed framework enables efficient evaluation of spin torques while capturing the nonlinear and spatially extended interactions generated by itinerant electrons. We benchmark the method on representative metallic magnetic systems exhibiting collinear, noncollinear, and noncoplanar magnetic order. The learned force fields accurately reproduce electronically generated spin torques and yield nonequilibrium spin dynamics in excellent agreement with direct electronic simulations. Our results establish graph neural networks as a powerful framework for machine-learned magnetic force fields, providing a pathway toward predictive large-scale simulations of nonequilibrium magnetism across multiple length and time scales.
summary: This paper presents a Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework designed to overcome computational bottlenecks in simulating spin dynamics in metallic magnets. The GNN learns the effective magnetic energy functional directly from electronic structure calculations, allowing for efficient prediction of complex spin torques and non-equilibrium behavior. This establishes GNNs as a powerful tool for large-scale simulations of itinerant magnetism.
main_problem: Developing computationally efficient methods to simulate complex spin dynamics in metallic magnets, which are bottlenecked by repeatedly solving underlying electronic structure problems during time evolution.
main_result: The proposed GNN framework accurately reproduces electronically generated spin torques and yields non-equilibrium spin dynamics that agree excellently with direct electronic simulations.
method: A Graph Neural Network (GNN) is introduced to learn the effective magnetic energy functional directly from electronic calculations, analogous to machine-learned interatomic potentials.
model_or_system: The system involves metallic magnets exhibiting itinerant electron-mediated interactions. The model focuses on learning the effective magnetic energy functional governing spin dynamics across various magnetic orders (collinear, noncollinear).
key_observables: Effective magnetic fields and spin torques; non-equilibrium spin dynamics.
important_parameters: The framework is applicable to systems exhibiting long-ranged, highly nonlinear interactions dependent on the instantaneous spin configuration.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that encoding local descriptors via message passing can capture complex many-body interactions and approximates the preservation of global SO(3) spin-rotation symmetry.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the GNN architecture, showing initialization from symmetry-preserving features, node updates aggregating neighbor information, and edge updates using endpoint site data.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the GNN framework by detailing its graph construction (nodes/edges), the message-passing mechanism for updating local descriptors while preserving symmetries, benchmarking it against known electronic calculations to validate spin torque reproduction, and finally applying it to large-scale non-equilibrium simulations.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the core methodology—using ML potentials derived from first principles to simulate complex many-body dynamics efficiently—is highly relevant for simulating open quantum systems or strongly interacting particle ensembles where direct time evolution is intractable.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic illustration of the graph-neural-network architecture. (a) The magnetic lattice is represented as a graph whose node and edge embeddings are initialized from symmetry-preserving spin features and subsequently refined through successive graph-neural-network layers. (b) Node-update operation, in which information from neighboring sites and connecting bonds is aggregated to generate an updated node embedding. (c) Edge-update operation, in which the bond embedding is updated using the existing edge feature together with information from the two endpoint sites.

FIG. 5. Further benchmark of the GNN force field for the non- coplanar tetrahedral phase. (a) Characteristic chiral-domain size L(t) as a function of time obtained from direct electronic simulations and GNN-based spin dynamics. The learned force field accurately reproduces the previously reported approxi- mately linear coarsening law L(t) ∼t. (b) Chirality cor- relation function C(r, t) plotted against the scaled distance r/L(t). The collapse of data at different times demonstrates dynamical scaling during chiral-domain coarsening. Together, these results show that the GNN force field faithfully captures the large-scale nonequilibrium dynamics of the chiral phase.
